reactions.name: Addition of HBr to an alkene

mechanism.summary: Protonation gives the more stable carbocation, then Br⁻ attacks.

traps: Markovnikov vs anti-Markovnikov (peroxide effect) — check for HBr + peroxide

mechanism.summary: Hydroxide attacks the electrophilic carbon, displacing halide.

reactions.name: Oxidation of a 1° alcohol to an aldehyde

mechanism.summary: PCC stops oxidation at the aldehyde stage (unlike KMnO4/K2Cr2O7).

traps: PCC does not over-oxidise to the acid — that needs KMnO4/K2Cr2O7

reactions.name: Oxidation of an aldehyde to an acid

mechanism.summary: Aldehyde is readily oxidised further to the carboxylic acid.

traps: Ketones resist this oxidation (no H on the carbonyl carbon)

mechanism.summary: Protonated acid attacked by the alcohol; loss of water gives the ester.

traps: Reversible — excess alcohol or removing water drives it forward

mechanism.summary: Hydride transfer to the carbonyl carbon, then protonation.

traps: NaBH4 does not reduce esters, acids or amides — LiAlH4 does

mechanism.summary: Anti-periplanar elimination of H and X gives the alkene (Zaitsev product favoured).

traps: Solvent decides the pathway: aqueous KOH → substitution, alcoholic KOH → elimination

mechanism.summary: Poisoned Pd catalyst stops hydrogenation at the cis-alkene.
Initiation, propagation, termination — a radical-chain halogenation.

traps: Statistically/stability-weighted mixture of products — not selective

reactions.name: Conversion of an alcohol to a haloalkane

mechanism.summary: PBr3 converts the poor leaving group –OH into a good one.
Protonation gives the more stable carbocation, then water attacks.

traps: Carbocation rearrangement is possible with 2° substrates

mechanism.summary: Protonated alcohol is attacked by a second alcohol molecule.

traps: At 170°C the same reagent instead eliminates to the alkene

mechanism.summary: Ammonia displaces halide; excess NH3 limits over-alkylation.

traps: Without excess NH3 this over-alkylates to 2°/3° amines and quaternary salts

mechanism.summary: Hydroxide attacks the carbonyl; the alkoxide leaving group is protonated on work-up.

traps: Base-mediated hydrolysis is irreversible (forms the carboxylate)

reactions.name: Addition of excess HBr to an alkyne

mechanism.summary: Two successive Markovnikov additions give the geminal dihalide.
The carbanion-like methyl adds to the carbonyl; acidic work-up protonates the alkoxide.

traps: Any acidic H (–OH, –NH, –COOH, terminal alkyne) destroys RMgX

mechanism.summary: AlCl3 generates the isopropyl carbocation, which the arene ring attacks.

traps: Carbocation rearrangement is possible — watch the alkyl halide/alkene used

mechanism.summary: Autoxidation to the hydroperoxide, then acid-catalysed rearrangement/cleavage giving phenol and acetone.

traps: Gives two products — phenol AND a ketone (acetone)

mechanism.summary: Hydroxylamine condenses with the carbonyl, losing water.
Cyanide adds to the carbonyl carbon.
FeBr3 polarises Br2; the ring attacks the electrophilic bromine.

traps: Isopropyl is an ortho/para director — this gives cumene a second outgoing branch, so it auto-resolves to Branched
Neither compound touches a major node, so §2.3 hides this reaction and both nodes from the graph — check the reaction list's warning group instead
